# Module 6 Lab: TimeGPT {.smaller}

```{r data_prep}
#| echo: false
aus_wine <- read_csv(
  here::here("data/AustralianWines.csv"),
  na = "*",
  col_types = cols(Rose = col_number()),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  fill(Rose, .direction = "down") |>
  mutate(Month = mdy(str_replace(Month, '-', '-01-')))

wines <- aus_wine |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -Month, names_to = 'Varietal', values_to = 'Sales') |>
  mutate(Month = yearmonth(Month)) |>
  as_tsibble(index = Month, key = Varietal)

wines |>
  autoplot(Sales) +
  labs(
    title = "Australian Wine Sales",
    y = "Sales (thousands of liters)"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~Varietal, nrow = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  theme(legend.position = "none") # hide legend
```


TimeGPT[@garza2023timegpt1] is Nixtla's foundation model for time series forecasting that can be accessed via their API. It is a large language model (LLM) trained on 1 million time series and can be used for zero-shot forecasting of new time series.

## Getting Started with TimeGPT {.smaller}

: Write code and instructions to predict all months of 1994 of the Wines dataset for all varietals, using TimeGPT.

Positron Assistant: I'll help you set up TimeGPT to predict all months of 1994 for all wine varietals. TimeGPT is Nixtla's foundation model for time series forecasting that can be accessed via their API.

## Setup Instructions {.smaller}

:::: column
### 1. Install Required Packages

First, install the necessary packages:

```         
# Install nixtlar package for TimeGPT access
install.packages("nixtlar")

# Load required libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(fpp3)
library(nixtlar)
library(gt)
```

::: fragment
### 2. Get TimeGPT API Key

1.  Go to <https://dashboard.nixtla.io/>
2.  Sign up for a free account
3.  Get your API token from the dashboard

##

![](images/nixtla-subscription.png)

## 3. Data Preparation

```{r}
# Prepare training data (through December 1993)
wines_train <- wines |>
  filter_index(. ~ '1993 Dec') |>
  mutate(Month = as.Date(Month)) |>  # Convert to Date for TimeGPT
  as_tibble()
```

TimeGPT requires a `tibble` (it doesn't use `tsibble`) with columns for unique ID, time, and target variable.

## 4. Generate TimeGPT Forecasts {.smaller}

```{r}
#| output-location: column
# If you want to rerun the forecast, set use_stored_results to FALSE
use_stored_results <- TRUE
timegpt_forecasts_rds <- here::here("labs/lab6-timegpt-forecasts.RDS")

if (use_stored_results & file.exists(timegpt_forecasts_rds)) {
  timegpt_forecasts <- read_rds(here::here(timegpt_forecasts_rds))
} else {
  # Generate forecasts for all varietals for 1994 (12 months)
  timegpt_forecasts <- nixtla_client_forecast(
    df = wines_train,
    h = 12, # 12 months ahead
    freq = "MS", # Monthly start frequency
    id_col = "Varietal", # "unique_id",
    time_col = "Month", # "ds",
    target_col = "Sales", # "y",
    level = c(80, 95) # Confidence intervals
  )
  # Save results to avoid repeated API calls
  write_rds(timegpt_forecasts, here::here("labs/lab6-timegpt-forecasts.RDS"))
}

# View results
head(timegpt_forecasts)
```

Change `use_stored_results` to `FALSE` or delete `.../labs/lab6-timegpt-forecasts.RDS` to call the service. The results are saved to an RDS file to avoid repeated API calls.

## 5. Process and Visualize Results {.smaller}

```{r}
#| output-location: column
#| figure-height: 5
# Convert back to tsibble format for analysis
timegpt_results <- timegpt_forecasts |>
  mutate(Month = yearmonth(Month)) |>
  rename(Sales = TimeGPT) |>
  as_tsibble(index = Month, key = Varietal)

# Create comparison plot
wines |>
  filter_index('1992 Jan' ~ '1994 Dec') |>
  autoplot(Sales) +
  geom_ribbon(
    data = timegpt_results,
    aes(ymin = `TimeGPT-lo-95`, ymax = `TimeGPT-hi-95`),
    alpha = 0.2, color = NA
  ) +
  autolayer(timegpt_results, Sales, size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~Varietal, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") 
```

## 6. Calculate Accuracy Metrics {.smaller}

```{r}
#| output-location: column
# Convert to forecast object format
timegpt_forecast_obj <- timegpt_results |>
  select(Month, Varietal, Sales) |>
  rename(.mean = Sales) |>
  mutate(dist = distributional::dist_normal(.mean, 1)) |> # Add fake distribution
  as_fable(response = "Sales", distribution = dist)

# Calculate accuracy for each varietal
accuracy_results <- timegpt_forecast_obj |>
  accuracy(wines)

make_gt <- function(df, header = "Accuracy Table") {
  df |>
    gt() |>
    tab_header(header) |>
    fmt_number(columns = c(RMSE, MAE), decimals = 1) |>
    fmt_number(columns = MAPE, decimals = 2) 
}

# Display accuracy table
timegpt_gt <- accuracy_results |>
  select(Varietal, RMSE, MAE, MAPE) |>
  arrange(Varietal) |>
  make_gt('Accuracy of TimeGPT Model') 
timegpt_gt
```

## ARIMA comparison: {.smaller}

```{r}
# Fit log transformed ARIMA models
arima_gt <- wines |>
  filter_index(. ~ '1993 Dec') |>
  model(
    arima = ARIMA(Sales)
  ) |>
  forecast(h = "1 year") |>
  accuracy(wines) |>
  select(Varietal, RMSE, MAE, MAPE) |>
  arrange(Varietal) |>
  make_gt('Accuracy of auto-ARIMA Model') 

```
